pr_title: I2S_MCUX: Fixup I2S MCUX Audio PLL Rate Calculation and Reg Writes
pr_body:
This PR Fixes the Audio PLL Rate Calculation (there was an additional
divide / 8 which is not necessary and does not appear in similar
calculations in example code from the SDK).

Additionally, it adjusts the SAI .dtsi to more correctly configure the
mclk rate, and adds comments specifying what the regististers mean.

Signed-off-by: Nickolas Lapp <nickolaslapp@gmail.com>

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45800

issue_context.title: Clock control settings for MCUX Audio Clock are Incorrect
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Audio PLL Clock Rate calculation for the I2S Clock is incorrect, resulting in incorrect downstream clocks (for example I2S MCLK). Additionally, the PLL configuration for NXP RT parts configures the PLL settings outside of their allowable ranges according to the datasheet.

This affects:
- MCUX Clock Control Driver when using the Audio PLL
- IMX RT Parts configuring the SAI module in DTS

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Run the sample I2S test code on a compatible NXP RT part:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/main/tests/drivers/i2s/i2s_api

1. west build -p auto -b mimxrt1060_evk tests/drivers/i2s/i2s_api
2. Probe the MCLK output line with a scope or logic analyzer and measure the MClk frequency
3. Compare it to the calculated MCLK rate (from the driver: [here](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/2dc866fa487ba524b426adc453d028bdd7aaa4e2/drivers/i2s/i2s_mcux_sai.c#L448))
4. Notice the measured value and the calculated value do not agree.

**Expected behavior**
The calculated mclk rate should match the actual produced rate and the driver should set up the PLL according to datasheet specifications.

**Impact**
I2S cannot be correctly configured on RT parts.

review_comments: From the RM: The Audio PLL goes directly through 2 dividers, but no automatic DIV/8 is needed. This is also backed up by example driver code from the MCU Expresso SDK Builder.
thanks for correcting this.  Yes, the DIV/8 here should be removed
